title: Counterintelligence Technician (CI Tech)
raw_text:
8-351L. MOS 351L--Counterintelligence Technician (CI Tech)
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. AR 381-14 for SQI W.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Pam 611-21 and AR 381-20
   c. MOS 351L. MOS 351L is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is 35L.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) K--Polygraph Examiner.
        (4) P--Parachutist.
        (5) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (6) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
        (7) W--Technical Surveillance Countermeasure Technician.
   e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
warrant officer MOS).
         (1) 1D--Digital Media Collector (Personnel Only).
         (2) N7—Strategic Debriefer (Effective 201410)
         (3) J5-- CI Digital Threat Investigator.
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Be a U.S. citizen.
              (b) Possess a security eligibility of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access to
sensitive compartmented information (SCI).
              (c) Complete the Counterintelligence Technician MI Warrant Officer Basic Course
(WOBC).
        (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
              (b) Complete the resident MI Warrant Officer Advanced Course (WOAC).
        (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
              (b) Complete Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
        (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(3).
              (b) Complete Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
   g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
              (a) Directs CI Operations and Investigations as the principal advisor to the Command
and staff on CI and other intelligence Operations, training, policies and procedures.
              (b) Manages CI support to the Military Decision Making Process (MDMP).
              (c) Employs internal and external capabilities and integrates analysis and automation
ISO CI Operations.
              (d) Conducts all CI activities IAW applicable laws and policies.
              (e) Serves as a Senior CI Technician responsible for areas of operation within tactical
and operational environments worldwide.
              (f) Performs duties in support of the Threat Awareness and Reporting Program
(TARP) and unit Covering Agent Program (CAP) to provide CI Assistance, knowledge, and
reporting procedures.
              (g) Performs evidence custodian duties; directs the CI application process and
conducts CI mission management.
              (h) May serve as a CI Team Chief.
              (i) May serve as OMT Chief.
              (j) May serve as BCT S2X CI Tech
              (k) May serve as CI Field Office/Investigations Team Leader.
        (2) CW3--
              (a) Directs and performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
              (b) Directs and supervises all CI elements, activities, special investigative, and
collection techniques in Operational and Strategic environments worldwide
              (c) Provides CI technical control, oversight, and management
             (d) Conducts CI operational coordination with joint, intergovernmental, and
multinational partners.
             (e) May serve as a Doctrine Writer.
             (f) May serve as a Detachment Commander.
             (g) May serve as an instructor at the WOCC, or at 111th MI BDE.
             (h) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
             (i) May serve as a Doctrine or Capabilities Developer.
        (3) CW4--
             (a) Manages, directs and performs duties shown in paragraph g(1) and g(2).
             (b) Directs and supervises all CI elements, activities, and special investigative, and
collection techniques in Operational and Strategic environments worldwide.
             (c) Provides CI technical control, oversight, and management.
             (d) Conducts CI operational coordination with joint, intergovernmental, and
multinational partners.
             (e) Serves as the principal advisor to senior staff members, decision, and policy
makers.
             (f) Provides advice and assistance to the Commander/Senior Intelligence officer on
all CI capabilities, activities, and policies and other intelligence operations.
             (g) Develops and plans all CI operations IAW applicable laws and policies.
             (h) May serve as a Doctrine Writer.
             (i) May serve as a Detachment Commander.
             (j) May serve as an instructor at the WOCC, or at 111th MI BDE.
             (k) May serve on the Joint or Combined Staff.
             (l) May serve as a Doctrine or Capabilities Developer.
             (m) May serve as the HRC MI WO Assignments Manager.                       (4) CW5--
             (a) MI CW5s are proficient in the duties described in the duties paragraphs of one or
more MI WO MOSs.
             (b) MI CW5s are branch technical experts and master-level technical and tactical
experts who perform the primary duties of technical leader, manager, multidiscipline intelligence
integrator, and advisor.
             (c) Provide direction, guidance, resources, assistance, and supervision necessary for
subordinates to perform their duties.
             (d) Provide leader development, talent and lifecycle management, mentorship,
advice, and counsel to enlisted Soldiers, warrant officers, and branch officers and have special
warrant officer leadership and representation responsibilities within their respective commands
             (e) Primarily support division, corps, echelons above corps, and major command
operations.
             (f) Advise commanders and branch assignment managers on the assignments and
placement of Military Intelligence warrant officers world-wide.
             (g) Provide essential advice to commanders on warrant officer issues and perform
other officer level duties as required consistent with senior staff officer responsibilities.
             (h) May serve as the Senior WO advisor in MOS immaterial (011A) billets based on
technical knowledge and understanding of Army and Joint doctrine.
             (i) May serve on the Army Staff.
             (j) May serve as a Capabilities Branch Chief.
             (k) May serve as the MI WO Proponent.
             (l) May serve as the CCWO of the MI Branch.
             (m) MI Senior Field Grade Warrant Officers must have competed the WO Senior
Service Education Course prior to nomination for specified CW5 billets
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate.
        (2) A physical profile of 222211.
        (3) Have normal color discrimination with corrected vision per one of the following three
categories of the good eye, bad eye categories: 20/40-20/70; 20/30-20/100; or, 20/20/400,
         (4) Have hearing wherein sound amplitude in one ear does not exceed 45 decibels at
frequencies 250, 500, 1000, and 2000 CPS (HZ) or 65 decibels at frequency 4000.
        (5) Qualifying Scores
              A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) – 120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) –
350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 120 lbs, and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 36 shuttles in Physical
Demands Category “Moderate” (Gold).
        (6) The following grade codes are used to code positions into one of four definable skill
levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The
grades are listed in the following standards of grade tables:
             (a) Table 8-351L-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
             (b) Table 8-351L-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
